clue.text: It may come before and after landing

definitions.text: It may come before and after landing

parts.words: It may come before and after landing
parts.note: a staircase has a run of steps leading up to a landing and another leading on from it, while an aircraft's journey ends in a touchdown

explanation.surface: An air traveller's remark about the journey either side of touching down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' suggests an aeroplane, but the main reading is a staircase: a set of stairs comes before a landing and another comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of stairs between floors or landings is called by this name, as is a journey by air.

clue.text: Good person has articles about New Zealand verse

parts.note: a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: about means the two articles sit around the country's abbreviation

parts.note: A and A are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A virtuous figure writes poetry with pieces about New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good person' is the crossword convention ST, for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lines forming a unit of a poem is a verse, a stanza.

clue.text: Second simpleton self-satisfied

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool, a simpleton

explanation.surface: The runner-up fool is pleased with himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smug is complacently pleased with themselves, a close synonym.

clue.text: One might say this very much as an expression of gratefulness

definitions.text: One might say this very much as an expression of gratefulness

parts.words: One might say this very much as an expression of gratefulness
parts.note: the familiar phrase of thanks is often followed by 'very much'

explanation.walkthrough: The clue hides the stock phrase of thanks inside its own wording: add 'very much' and you have the full expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard way of expressing gratitude in English.

clue.text: Give rage in order to afflict

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Making someone angry is a way of troubling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges GIVE RAGE; 'to' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict someone is to distress or wrong them, which is to aggrieve them.

clue.text: Greatest ever intoxicated state, this level has never been reached before

definitions.meaning: playful reading: the most stoned anyone has ever been, a high to beat all highs

definitions.text: this level has never been reached before
definitions.meaning: a record peak, as of a share price or temperature

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on 'high' meaning intoxicated; the second is the ordinary financial or statistical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a record peak, never before attained, and jokingly the greatest drug-induced state.

clue.text: Bloomer having neat edge

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox is a neat
a lip is the edge or rim of something

explanation.surface: A gaffe made with a tidy border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it means something that blooms, a flower; 'neat' is the archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a primula, a flowering plant, so it is a bloomer.

clue.text: Painfully sensitive flesh lasting a short time

definitions.meaning: the tender flesh under a fingernail, as in 'cut to the' ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the sensitive flesh beneath the nails and also means brief or speedy.

clue.text: Cunning but not to start with having information on gas

indicators.note: not to start with means the opening letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: foxy means sly, cunning
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone sly, though not initially, being briefed about a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start with' removes F from FOXY.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is a chemical element that is a gas at room temperature, an example.

clue.text: Urges one to become bountiful

indicators.note: the letters of the two words become something else, a reworked arrangement

explanation.surface: A call for someone to be openhanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Bountiful and generous both describe giving freely, a synonym.

clue.text: Avert filly travelling in depressed area in Africa

indicators.note: travelling signals that the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning away a young mare on a journey through Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed area' means a sunken stretch of land, not a gloomy region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Rift Valley is a long sunken trough running through East Africa.

clue.text: I will leave Russian front

indicators.note: will leave means the I named before it goes from the Russian name

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name, standing for a Russian

explanation.surface: A speaker announcing they will depart the Russian front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian front' reads as one military phrase, but 'Russian' gives IVAN and 'front' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The van is the vanguard, the leading part or front of an army or procession.

clue.text: Endless good fortune concerning money

indicators.note: endless means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: luck is good fortune
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Unending luck in financial matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is a somewhat disparaging word for money, a synonym.

clue.text: Cut out of wet chalk

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken from within the words wet chalk

explanation.surface: Carving a shape out of damp chalk.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface with acid or a tool.

clue.text: Supposed to have done some magic round European court

indicators.note: round means the magic verb goes around the abbreviations

parts.note: conjured means performed a magic trick

explanation.surface: A conjuror's supposed performance in front of a European court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supposed to' reads as 'meant to', but 'Supposed' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjectured means guessed or supposed without firm evidence, a synonym.

clue.text: Baker upset after cancelled delivery

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the word for cancelled

parts.note: an event called off is cancelled, so off

indicators.note: upset signals the word baker is knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A baker distressed after his order is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: An off break is a cricket delivery spun by the bowler so it turns into a right-handed batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a delivery is a ball bowled, and an off break is one type.

clue.text: Jo prayed about hazard

indicators.note: about indicates the letters are turned around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Jo said prayers concerning some danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is danger or risk, the same as hazard.

clue.text: Soldiers drinking unknown whisky

indicators.note: drinking means the soldiers take the unknown inside them

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Troops downing an unknown spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whisky distilled mostly from rye grain, an example.

clue.text: Smooth learner in orchestra

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter inside the musical group

parts.note: a band is an orchestra
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A trainee playing smoothly in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland can mean suave and unruffled in manner, or mild and even, hence smooth.

clue.text: Quiet and mischievous being in part of library?

parts.note: sh is the sound used to call for quiet
an elf is an impish creature

explanation.surface: A silent sprite lurking in the library, where silence is demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Books in a library sit on ledges, so one is a part of the library.

clue.text: Symbol of Conservative and most of opposition?

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: the left is the political opposition to the Conservatives

explanation.surface: A political emblem combining the Tories with most of their rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the musical symbol fixing the pitch of the stave.

clue.text: Finished week taking on number too heavy

indicators.note: taking on means the week adds the number after it

parts.note: over means finished
eight is a number

explanation.surface: After a finished week of feasting, someone has put on too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweight means weighing more than is healthy or allowed, too heavy.

clue.text: Careful to adopt Catholic slogan

indicators.note: to adopt means the cautious word takes the abbreviation into itself

parts.note: wary means careful
RC is Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Taking up a Catholic motto with caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallying cry or slogan shouted in battle or used in a campaign.

clue.text: In action? Certainly

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A question about being busy, met with firm agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is used as emphatic agreement, meaning certainly or truly.

clue.text: Advance in French vehicle going round centre of Bourges

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: going round means the vehicle surrounds the central letter

parts.note: a coach is a vehicle

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the town name

explanation.surface: A French bus travelling around central Bourges.
explanation.walkthrough: Bourges is a city in central France; its middle letter is R.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to advance gradually beyond proper limits.

clue.text: Had old money dropped repeatedly in ditch

indicators.note: repeatedly means the result is used twice
dropped means the old money is removed from had

parts.note: D was the symbol for the old British penny

explanation.surface: Someone who had old cash kept dropping it into a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the penny in pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch that acts as a boundary without spoiling a view.

clue.text: Puzzle that might be draining

definitions.meaning: a coarse sieve, which lets earth or water drain through

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a conundrum, and also a large sieve used to sift soil, so something that drains.

clue.text: Jack perhaps clearer as a cheat

parts.note: a jack is one example of a playing card
sharper means clearer, as a sharper image

explanation.surface: A man named Jack comes across more lucidly as a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the jack as one example of a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharper is someone who cheats at cards, a kind of swindler.
